content.user_title: Structure TypeScript Systems With Architecture Patterns
content.value_statement: AI-generated TypeScript code often drifts without clear architectural boundaries. This skill provides reusable pattern guidance for DDD, Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and POM testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains Domain-Driven Design concepts with TypeScript entity, value object, and repository examples.
Shows Clean Architecture layers for domain, application, adapter, and infrastructure code.
Describes Hexagonal Architecture with ports, adapters, and swappable integration examples.
Provides Page Object Model guidance for Playwright and Cypress end-to-end tests.
Compares patterns and recommends combinations for common project types.
limitations: It provides documentation and examples, not a runnable framework or generator.
Examples are simplified and need adaptation for production security and error handling.
It focuses on TypeScript projects and may not fit other language ecosystems.
It does not inspect an existing codebase or enforce architecture automatically.

use_cases.title: Plan a New TypeScript Backend
use_cases.description: Select DDD, Clean Architecture, or Hexagonal Architecture before asking an AI assistant to generate features.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Use the pattern guidance to check whether generated code keeps business logic, infrastructure, and controllers separate.

use_cases.title: Create Maintainable E2E Tests
use_cases.description: Apply Page Object Model examples to produce reusable Playwright or Cypress page classes and focused test scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between DDD, Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Page Object Model for this TypeScript project: [describe project].

prompt_templates.title: Design Layer Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the Clean Architecture layers for this TypeScript feature: [feature]. List domain objects, use cases, adapters, and infrastructure responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Define Ports and Adapters
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hexagonal Architecture for this service: [service]. Define core ports, adapter responsibilities, and test doubles for each external integration.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor With Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript module against DDD and Clean Architecture. Propose refactoring steps and Page Object Model tests for the user workflows.

output_examples.input: Design a checkout feature for a TypeScript API using Clean Architecture.
output: Domain entities and value objects are identified first.
Use cases define order confirmation, payment authorization, and inventory reservation.
Repository and payment interfaces isolate database and provider details.

output_examples.input: Create a maintainable login test strategy for a Playwright project.
output: A LoginPage object owns selectors and page actions.
Tests call intent-based methods such as login and verify page state.
Assertions stay in test files instead of page objects.

output_examples.input: Refactor a service with direct database and API calls.
output: Core business rules move into domain objects or use cases.
Database and API calls move behind ports and adapters.
Unit tests cover core logic with fake implementations.

best_practices: Start with domain language and responsibilities before asking the AI assistant to write code.
Generate one layer or adapter at a time so boundaries remain clear.
Use tests and code review to confirm that generated code follows the selected pattern.
anti_patterns: Do not mix business rules, HTTP handling, and database calls in one generated file.
Do not expose page locators directly when using Page Object Model tests.
Do not apply every pattern at once when a simpler structure is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill generate application code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that improve prompts for AI coding tools.

faq.question: Which TypeScript architecture patterns are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Domain-Driven Design, Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Page Object Model testing.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for AI-assisted coding workflows across these tools.

faq.question: Is this only for backend services?
faq.answer: No. Backend architecture is the main focus, but Page Object Model guidance supports frontend end-to-end tests.

faq.question: Does it replace human architecture review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure AI output, but teams should still review design, security, and production readiness.

faq.question: When should I avoid these patterns?
faq.answer: Avoid heavy layering for small scripts, prototypes, or features where simple modules meet the need.
